about.title: El Cajon Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A fall rarely feels like a legal matter in the moment. You are on the ground in a grocery aisle off Broadway, a stairwell in an apartment complex, or a parking lot along Fletcher Parkway, and the first thoughts are about pain and embarrassment, not paperwork. Yet in California, whether you can recover for that fall usually comes down to one question: did the property owner know, or should they have known, about the hazard and fail to fix it or warn you? That is called notice, and proving it takes evidence that disappears quickly. El Cajon is home to about 103,679 people spread across older commercial strips on E Main Street, newer retail, and many apartment communities, and each kind of property brings its own set of responsibilities for whoever controls it. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles premises liability claims in San Diego County and works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why El Cajon Fall Victims Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Attorneys who know how to prove notice
items.desc: Under California law, you generally have to show the owner knew or should have known about the hazard and did nothing. The attorneys in our network know where to look for inspection logs, prior complaints, and maintenance records that establish that.

items.title: Fast action on video and evidence
items.desc: Store and apartment surveillance footage is often overwritten within days. A quick connection to an attorney means a preservation request can go out before the recording of your fall is gone.

items.title: Deadlines and fault handled correctly
items.desc: Most California premises claims carry a two-year deadline, but a fall on public property comes with a far shorter window. California also uses pure comparative fault, so being partly to blame reduces a claim rather than ending it, and the attorney you are matched with will explain how that applies to you.

items.question: I fell on a cracked sidewalk in El Cajon. Is the city responsible, and does that change my deadline?
items.answer: It might be, depending on who owns and maintains that stretch of sidewalk and whether the City of El Cajon or another public entity knew about the defect. Claims against a public entity in California follow a much shorter timeline than the usual two years, generally requiring a formal government claim within about six months of the injury. Because that clock runs quickly, it is worth talking with an attorney soon after a fall on any public property.

items.question: The store told me they don't have video of my fall. What can I do?
items.answer: Do not take that answer as final. Many El Cajon businesses keep footage only for a short period, so an attorney will typically send a written preservation demand right away and ask for camera locations, incident reports, and cleaning schedules. Your own photos of the hazard, the names of witnesses, and the clothing and shoes you wore that day also help fill in the picture.

items.question: I was looking at my phone when I slipped. Can I still bring a claim?
items.answer: Yes. California applies pure comparative fault, which means your recovery is reduced by your share of responsibility instead of being wiped out. If the owner should have known about a spill or a loose mat and did not address it, their share of the fault still counts. An independent attorney can review the facts and give you an honest read on how fault is likely to be divided.
